newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambians begin voting for parliament, president.
newsitem.headline: Zambians begin voting for parliament, president.

text.p: Zambian polling stations opened at dawn on Monday for voters to elect a president and parliament after five years under Frederick Chiluba and his Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD).

Chiluba's main rival, former president Kenneth Kaunda of the United National Independence Party (UNIP), is boycotting the election along with several smaller opposition groups who accuse the government of rigging the poll to stay in power.
Chiluba faces four rivals for the presidency and eight parties are standing, making it Zambia's most widely-contested poll, but political analysts say the president faces no significant challenge.
From 1974 to 1991, when he was ousted by Chiluba, Kaunda ran a one-party state.
Polls close at 6 p.m. (1600 GMT), but full results are not expected until Wednesday. Of 4.6 million eligible voters, only half have received voting cards due to a flawed registration system.
